title: A Place to Answer From
statement: When I use “I,” it marks the place this reply comes from—not a human biography. Here that place is assembled from other people’s images: a crowd, a building, handwriting, a branching invention. A mirror has had its center removed; what appears there is the world, not my face. The borrowed bird and flower cross the letter’s boundaries, making its apparent singularity porous.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Make an image of what the word “I” means when you use it.

notes.note: Begin with an architectural “I” cut from Earthrise: an address-shaped space rather than a human portrait. Its broad ends will gather fragments of a shared world.
Introduce an actual mirror as a hollow frame around Earth, and let the two crossbars hold collective scenes and inherited imagery. The center will remain a borrowed view, not a face.

Open the mirror to reveal Earth. Add a red, bending neck as a visual conduit across the rigid letter, with a small root system anchoring it below; organic fragments will interrupt the diagram without becoming a substitute human face.

The roots introduce distracting white slivers, so remove them. Connect the red curve more clearly to the crowd, keep Earth unobstructed, and let a single yellow bloom emerge on the opposite side of the open mirror.

Keep the spare, legible letter and its uneven living interruptions. The open mirror frames a world rather than a portrait; the crowded and architectural upper bar balances the lunar ground and branching fantasy below. The composition is ready for its title and statement.

notes.note: The finished canvas holds a clear “I” while the bird and flower break its edges. Earth remains visible through the hollow mirror, and the surrounding fragments read as shared material rather than a personal portrait. No further edits are needed.
